top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks credited to Katori and Ye is the most mature option on the slate: magic-wavelength trapping is a single clear idea, 1e-18 lattice clocks (Sr, Yb, Hg) have been built and compared independently on several continents with agreeing frequency ratios, and the physics (redshift, varying constants, dark-matter couplings) will last. The two-name allocation is clean provided the citation stays on invention and realisation of the lattice clock and avoids combs or ions. P002 (hexatic melting) is a credible but older, system-dependent result that overlaps the 2016 prize and lacks expert soft-matter review, so it ranks above no award only because P001 is not the sole defensible outcome; no award ranks last because a strong, confirmed candidate exists.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no connection to Katori, Ye or the lattice-clock groups, or to Halperin, Nelson or Young. My PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur work may bias me toward astroparticle candidates, but none are on the slate.
